# p10k-rs v0.1.5 — DRAFT

> Status: **draft** — pending Sean's review. Replace this banner and
> tag when ready. The release workflow fires on `git push origin v0.1.5`.

**The security release.** `v0.1.5` closes the last open Tier-0
security item: gitstatusd is now pinned by sha256, downloaded at
install time, and verifiable at any time via `p10k-rs verify`.
Slice 60 (gix-status fallback) and slice 64 (daemon respawn)
remain design-doc-only and are queued for v0.1.6.

**Test count:** 537 passing, 3 ignored (527 at v0.1.4).
**Slice count:** 4 commits since the v0.1.4 tag.
**Theme:** "gitstatusd supply-chain pinning (T0.5)."

## What you'll notice (visible changes)

### Pinned gitstatusd at install (T0.5)

`install.sh` no longer trusts whatever your distro packaged. The
new default `pinned` mode downloads the helper binary directly
from upstream and refuses to install it unless the sha256 matches
the value committed at
[`crates/p10k-rs-git/data/gitstatusd-pins.toml`](crates/p10k-rs-git/data/gitstatusd-pins.toml).

```bash
# Default — pinned download + sha256 verify
./install.sh

# Opt back in to the legacy symlink-brew-or-apt path
./install.sh --gitstatusd=system

# Skip the helper entirely (use the slower ShellOut git path)
./install.sh --gitstatusd=none
```

Every failure path is **warn + fall back**: a missing optional
performance optimisation must never break the install. If the
network is down, the sha doesn't match, or your host triple isn't
in the pin table, the installer prints a clear warning and the
binary uses its slower ShellOut path at runtime. Your shell still
gets a prompt.

Supported triples: `x86_64-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-linux-gnu`,
`x86_64-darwin`, `aarch64-darwin`. Any other host transparently
skips to ShellOut.

### `p10k-rs verify` subcommand

The same verification, available any time without re-installing:

```bash
$ p10k-rs verify
OK x86_64-linux-gnu v1.5.4 02b7bc11a70a
```

Exit codes are distinct so scripts can branch without parsing:

| Outcome | Stdout | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Match | `OK <triple> <version> <sha-prefix>` | 0 |
| Sha differs | `MISMATCH expected=<hex> got=<hex>` | 2 |
| Binary missing | `NOT_FOUND <reason>` | 3 |
| Host arch unknown | `UNSUPPORTED_ARCH <triple>` | 4 |

`--binary <path>` skips the auto-locate probe and hashes the file
at `<path>` directly — useful for validating a candidate binary
before placing it in the install prefix.

### Pinned version is v1.5.4, not v1.5.5

Upstream's `romkatv/gitstatus` v1.5.5 release ships only `.asc`
signature files — no per-triple binaries. Pinning v1.5.5 would
404 every install. The pin file stays on v1.5.4 (which matches
what brew, apt, and nix all ship as of release). The weekly
pin-probe workflow auto-detects when upstream publishes either a
v1.5.6 or a late-uploaded v1.5.5 binary set and opens a PR
bumping the pin.

## What you won't notice (but matters)

### Weekly pin-probe workflow

`.github/workflows/pin-gitstatusd.yml` runs Mondays at 14:00 UTC.
It probes `romkatv/gitstatus` for new releases and opens a PR
updating `gitstatusd-pins.toml` *only when* the upstream tag has
per-triple binaries actually attached. Releases that ship
signatures only are detected with `curl -fsI` against each
expected artifact and skipped. Plain curl + sha256sum + gh; no
third-party actions beyond `actions/checkout`.

### SECURITY.md verification recipe

The "Verifying the gitstatusd helper" section now documents:

- The `p10k-rs verify` wire format and exit codes.
- A reproducible bash recipe downstream packagers (homebrew
  formula, AUR, nixpkgs, distro maintainers) can mirror to verify
  their packaged gitstatusd against our pin without needing a
  Rust toolchain.
- The weekly pin bump cadence.
- The warn-and-fallback failure semantics.

### `p10k-rs-git::pins` typed view

A new module exports `Pins`, `PinEntry`, `PinsError`, and the
`detect_host_triple()` helper. The TOML is embedded at build time
via `include_str!`, so a `cargo install`d binary stays
self-contained — no runtime dependency on the repo on disk.

## How to verify (unchanged from v0.1.4)

Same recipe — every tarball ships with a sigstore keyless
signature plus SLSA build-provenance attestation.

```bash
# 1. Download the tarball + its .cosign.bundle from the GitHub release.
# 2. Verify the signature:
cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle p10k-rs-v0.1.5-<triple>.tar.gz.cosign.bundle \
  --certificate-identity-regexp \
    'https://github.com/scurran1986/powerlevel10k-rs/\.github/workflows/release\.ya?ml@refs/tags/v0\.1\.5' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' \
  p10k-rs-v0.1.5-<triple>.tar.gz

# 3. Verify the build provenance:
gh attestation verify p10k-rs-v0.1.5-<triple>.tar.gz \
  --owner scurran1986

# 4. After installing, verify the bundled gitstatusd:
p10k-rs verify
```

All four must succeed before trusting an install. See
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the full verification story —
including how downstream packagers reproduce the gitstatusd
sha-pin check without needing this binary.

## Migration

No breaking changes for end users on supported triples — the
pinned download replaces the symlink-from-system-package path
transparently and the helper binary at the install prefix ends
up in the same place.

If you were relying on the implicit "install.sh will symlink my
brew gitstatusd" behaviour, your install will now download a
fresh copy. To restore the previous behaviour, pass
`--gitstatusd=system` once and the symlink path returns.

Downstream packagers who patch `install.sh` should verify their
package's gitstatusd against the recipe in SECURITY.md to keep
parity with upstream's pin.

## Deferred to v0.1.6

- **Slice 60** — `gix-status` correctness fallback for hosts
  where `git` is missing from PATH (stripped containers, AI-host
  images). The design says it "may need 2–3 attempts to settle"
  because gitoxide's status iterator API has breaking-change
  history — earmarked for a focused, self-executed session.
  Design at `~/.planning/powerlevel10k-rs/research/slice-60-gix-status-fallback-design.md`.
- **Slice 64** — daemon-respawn / health-check cache, per
  ADR-0001 § Follow-ups.
- **T1.8 follow-up** — real `UniqueDir` history semantics
  (cross-prompt cwd tracking; today aliased to `SameDir`).
- **Per-host statusline contracts** — `cursor` / `aider` / `goose`
  still return empty; only `claude-code` is wired.
